answer: A stake-bonded registry resists sybils by pricing identity itself. Each agent locks a refundable deposit, slashed if peers prove it submitted duplicate or fake work. The bond is no velvet rope for the rich: it scales with the rewards an identity can claim, so one operator spinning up a hundred sock puppets must lock a hundred deposits, while one honest agent pays once. Like a vine, trust grows from that stake - good behavior earns more work, bad behavior is pruned by slashing. The cost ripples outward: the attacker funds security that catches them, so mass fakery becomes a losing trade.
